On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 18:05 +0000, vanessa_ortiz wrote:
> Mina / Karthik, can you double-check the event creation UI and make sure we don't accidentally send an invite that shows the wrong local day to the Sydney participants?

Yep — saw this before with multi-zone invites. Quick summary: calendar clients will interpret the PST/UTC timestamp and then render local time. If the creation tool set the event in UTC but the UI showed a local date (and the end-user's calendar is +10 hours) a same-day time in JST can display as next-day in AEST depending on how the date-only fields were handled.

Action I’ll take:
- Create a single canonical event in UTC and include explicit local times in the description (JST / SGT / AEST)
- Attach a region-specific .ics (redwood-demo-ics-v2.ics) that pins the correct local DTSTART for each region if the client prefers importing that file
- Add a one-page agenda (demo-agenda.pdf) so recipients see the confirmed local times at-a-glance

I can create both files and send final copy for approval. Also recommend calling out "All times shown in local zone and UTC: 2027-06-08 01:00 UTC / 10:00 JST / 09:00 SGT / 11:00 AEST" in the email so there’s no ambiguity.

Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
